AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Chronic plantar heel pain (CPHP) is a significant, painful condition referring to a range of undifferentiated foot conditions that affect the heel of the foot.

AbstractText.Label: METHOD
AbstractText.content: Participants presenting with CPHP of more than 6 months' duration were recruited on a first through the door basis. Computer-Aided Design and Computer-Aided Manufactured (CAD-CAM) orthoses were designed and constructed for each participant, then dispensed as per normal practice. Pre- and postintervention assessment of pain was performed at baseline and after 6 weeks of use, utilizing the pain subset of the Foot Function Index (FFI).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: There was a significant reduction in the mean pain scores for all participants in all constructs of the FFI. Total FFI score was also significant ( P = .003).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: CAD-CAM orthoses have the potential to become a treatment modality of choice in CPHP since they have resulted in a significant improvement in heel pain after only 6 weeks' use.

AbstractText.Label: LEVELS OF EVIDENCE
AbstractText.content: Therapeutic, Level IV: Prospective, comparative trial.
